fields.meta_title: Product Recommendation Quiz Builder for Stores | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a free product recommendation quiz that picks a backpack, then build one that matches shoppers to products you stock.
fields.h1: Build a Product Recommendation Quiz for Your Store
fields.hero_description: Take the backpack quiz below, or build a product recommendation quiz that matches each shopper to a product you stock.
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the quiz, its matching rules, and the table behind them from one prompt. Describe a change to edit any part.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that point to your products

List the products or product types you want to recommend. Emergent builds the questions with every option tied to one of them, and changes any question you flag in a later prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Matches pulled from your live catalog

Connect your store or inventory tool through its API, and the result screen lists the products tagged for that match, with stock counts, instead of a fixed list typed into the quiz.
fields.feature_3:
One row for each completed quiz

The app stores each completed quiz in a database you own, with the product it matched, every answer, and an email when given. Sort by product to see which items the quiz sells most.
fields.feature_4:
Big-ticket matches sent to a person

Set a rule, such as a budget over $2,500, and the app sends a Slack or email alert to the staff member who handles that sale, with every answer the shopper gave on the quiz.
fields.feature_5:
A count of where shoppers quit

Ask for a dashboard beside the quiz, and it counts how many people start, how many finish, and which question each person quit on. Move or cut the question that loses the most.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code in GitHub

Run the quiz on your own domain or a subdomain of your store, included with Emergent and paid in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Shops Matching Customers to Products
fields.tab_content_1:
One north window, three plants in stock

Nora Ilves tells Sill and Stem's plant quiz that her apartment has one north window and that she is away two weekends a month. The result screen shows the 3 plants the shop tagged for low light and low water, pulled from its catalog with a stock count beside each. Her match is saved to the shop's customer table.
fields.tab_content_2:
A $3,200 gravel budget reaches the fitter

Riders who name a budget over $2,500 on Corvid Cycles' bike quiz get a fitting offer with their match. Sam Okafor picks gravel, 60-mile weekend rides, and $3,200. The fitter, Lucia Brandt, gets an email with every answer. She calls him before Saturday. Riders under $2,500 see in-stock bikes and a cart link.
fields.tab_content_3:
760 shoppers quit when asked for an email

In March, 3,200 shoppers started Ashgrove Kitchen Supply's pan quiz and 1,940 finished. The drop-off count put 760 of the quits at question 6, which asked for an email before showing the match. The shop moved the email ask to the result screen, below the pan, and made it optional.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which aisle holds a $40 building toy

Pinwheel Toys prints a QR code on a card by the register. Ruth Amsel scans it and answers 5 questions about her grandson, including his age, 7, what he likes, building, and her budget, $40. Her phone shows 3 building toys at $40 or less and the aisle each sits in. The quiz saves all 5 answers, with no name.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a product recommendation quiz that ends on an in-stock product, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the products before the questions
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask how they will use it
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Point every option at a product
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep hard limits out of the scoring
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the products or product groups the quiz can recommend, between three and six of them, and check each one is in stock. Questions come quickly once you know the destinations, since every option has to point at one of them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about the shopper's life, not your spec sheet: the light in the room, the roads they ride, the pans they burn. A shopper can answer those in a second, while a question about frame geometry or wattage invites a guess.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each option one product it scores for, and let every product win in at least two questions. Keep the options alike in length and tone, so no answer looks like the joke choice that people skip.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Treat budget, size, and age as filters, not points. A shopper with $40 to spend should never see a $90 match, however well it scored, so let the filter remove it before the result screen loads.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Under the product name, write one line that ties it to the answers: low light, away on weekends. Add a second choice for shoppers who want options, and link both straight to the product page or cart.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide what happens after the match
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the follow-up for each result: a cart link, an email to staff for a big-ticket match, or a saved row for the next newsletter. Put it in your prompt, and Emergent builds the routing along with the quiz.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Take the quiz once for each result
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the link goes live, take the quiz once per product, choosing the options that point to it, and confirm that product wins. Then open the saved row and any staff email to check the answers arrived intact.

faq_plan.q: What is a product recommendation quiz?
faq_plan.a: A product recommendation quiz is a short set of questions a store asks a shopper, scored so the answers point to one product or product group to buy. The quiz on this page asks seven questions about your days and names the backpack type that fits them.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a product recommendation quiz?
faq_plan.a: List the products you want to recommend, then describe the quiz in a prompt: the questions, which answers point to which product, and what the result screen shows. Emergent's AI survey builder drafts it along with the table behind it. Take it once for each result, then publish and share the link.

faq_plan.q: How does a product recommendation quiz connect to a store's product catalog?
faq_plan.hint: How to create product recommendation quiz for online store?
faq_plan.a: Through the API of the platform that holds the catalog. Each result carries a product tag, such as low light, and the result screen asks the catalog for in-stock items with that tag. Apps built on Emergent connect to any tool with an API, and the catalog stays the one list you update.

faq_plan.q: Can you send a product recommendation quiz in an email?
faq_plan.hint: How to embed product recommendation quiz in email?
faq_plan.a: Send it as a link. Put the first question in the email as a row of buttons, each one opening the quiz with that answer already chosen. The reader starts on question 2. A style quiz sent in a newsletter works the same way, and the click itself records the first answer.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a product recommendation quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for six to eight. That is enough to separate four or five products and short enough to finish on a phone in one sitting. Cut any question whose answers never change the result, and show a progress bar on every screen.

faq_plan.q: How does a product recommendation quiz decide which product to show?
faq_plan.a: It counts points. Each answer adds a point to one product, and the product with the most points at the end is the match. Count a question twice when it matters most, such as terrain on a bike quiz, and decide the tie rule before launch, such as the cheaper product wins.

faq_plan.q: How is a product recommendation quiz different from a quiz with right answers?
faq_plan.a: It has no right answers. A scored quiz, such as a vocabulary quiz, marks each answer correct or wrong and reports a score. A product recommendation quiz maps each answer to a product, and every path ends on something the shopper can buy.

faq_plan.q: What should a product recommendation quiz for gifts ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the person receiving the gift, not the buyer: their age, how they spend free time, and what they already own. Ask the budget last and use it as a filter. End on two or three picks instead of one, since the buyer is choosing for someone else.

faq_plan.q: Where should a product recommendation quiz go on a store's website?
faq_plan.a: Put it where shoppers stall: the home page, a collection page full of similar products, or the main menu for a quiz people come back to. A quiz built on Emergent can run on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

faq_plan.q: Can a product recommendation quiz show what customers want?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in part. Each finished quiz records the needs a shopper named and the product the answers pointed to. A run of matches for an item you barely stock is a buying signal. To learn whether a new product is wanted at all, ask current users with a product market fit survey. Emergent keeps every answer in a database you own.

quiz.title: Product Recommendation Quiz: Find Your Everyday Backpack
quiz.intro: Seven questions about your days and what you carry. Your result names the backpack type that fits, with the features to look for when you shop.

questions.text: How do you get to work or school most days?

options.text: Train or bus, then a short walk
I work from wherever I am traveling that month
On foot, with a trail most weekends
By bike, in any weather

questions.text: What has to fit inside on a normal day?

options.text: Three days of clothes
Water, snacks, and a rain shell
A change of clothes that must stay dry
A laptop, a charger, and lunch

questions.text: Where does the bag spend a rainy Tuesday?

options.text: On my back on a muddy path
Strapped on while I ride through puddles
Under my desk at the office
In an overhead bin

questions.text: Which part of a bag do you use most?

options.text: One big sealed space with no zippers
A padded laptop sleeve
A main section that opens flat like a suitcase
Side pockets for water bottles
A cracked laptop screen
A bag fee at the gate
Sore shoulders on a long climb
Soaked work clothes
A slim shape that passes as a carry-on
Bright colors and mesh panels
Reflective strips and a rolled top
Plain black that fits in at a meeting

questions.text: What is the longest regular stretch you carry this bag?

options.text: A 4-hour hike
A 10-mile ride each way
A full workday
A long weekend away

results.title: Commuter Backpack
results.description: Your answers lean toward a commuter backpack. Look for a padded laptop sleeve raised off the bottom of the bag, a quick-grab top pocket for keys and a transit card, and a strap that slides over a suitcase handle.

results.title: Carry-On Travel Pack
results.description: Your answers lean toward a travel pack sized as a carry-on. Look for a main section that unzips flat like a suitcase, compression straps, and a hip belt that tucks away. Check your airline's carry-on size before you buy.

results.title: Hiking Daypack
results.description: Your answers lean toward a hiking daypack. Look for a ventilated back panel, a padded hip belt, two side pockets that hold a bottle each, and a sleeve for a water reservoir.

results.title: Waterproof Roll-Top Pack
results.description: Your answers lean toward a waterproof roll-top pack. Look for a roll-top closure, welded seams, reflective strips for rides after dark, and a loop for a rear light.

plan.angle: The top 10 is quiz-app vendors (two Shopify quiz apps, a quiz-funnel tool, a pop-up tool) and listicles of quiz examples. This page lets a visitor take a full product recommendation quiz that names an everyday backpack type, then shows four shops wiring the result to something that sells: a plant shop's live catalog, a bike fitter's inbox, a cookware store's drop-off count, and a toy store's aisle map. Every answer is a row in a database the shop owns, and the FAQ covers catalog hookups, email sends, question counts, scoring, ties, gift finders, and result screens.
